extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office examiners; patent applicants, attorneys, and agents
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and examiner procedures for drawings, replacement sheets, annotated sheets, models/exhibits/specimens, and handling of new matter in U.S. patent applications as set forth in the MPEP and relevant CFR provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 CFR 1.84 for drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings and any changes to drawings must comply with 37 CFR 1.84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All changes to an application drawing must be in compliance with § 1.84 and submitted on a replacement sheet labeled in the top margin as 'Replacement Sheet' (or 'New Sheet' for new figures) pursuant to 37 CFR 1.121(d). Any replacement sheet shall include all of the figures appearing on the immediate prior version of the sheet, even if only one figure is amended. All changes to the drawings shall be explained, in detail, in either the drawing amendment or remarks section of the amendment paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: No holding objections in abeyance; timely correction required
rubrics_metrics.description: Objections to the drawings in a utility or plant application will not be held in abeyance and must be corrected before examination proceeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.85(a). A request to hold objections to the drawings in abeyance will not be considered a bona fide attempt to advance the application to final action. Applicant is required to submit acceptable corrected drawings within the time period set in the Office action; failure to take corrective action will result in abandonment of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement sheet labeling and content rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Replacement sheets must be labeled and must include all figures from the prior version of the sheet; new sheets labeled 'New Sheet'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each drawing sheet submitted after the filing date must be labeled in the top margin as either 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet' pursuant to 37 CFR 1.121(d). A replacement sheet must include all of the figures appearing on the immediate prior version of the sheet, even if only one figure is amended. The figure or figure number of an amended drawing should not be labeled as 'amended.' If a drawing figure is to be canceled, the appropriate figure must be removed from the replacement sheet and remaining figures renumbered with corresponding changes to the brief description of the several views of the drawings for consistency. Additional replacement sheets may be necessary to show renumbering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotated (marked-up) sheets requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When changes are made to drawings (other than minor matters), a marked-up copy including annotations indicating the changes must be provided and labeled 'Annotated Sheet'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A marked-up copy of any amended drawing figure, including annotations indicating the changes made, may be included and must be clearly labeled as 'Annotated Sheet' and presented in the amendment or remarks section that explains the change(s). When required by the examiner, a marked-up copy must be provided. Annotated sheets filed by an applicant and used for correction will not be returned and must be in ink or permanent prints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications may not be shown in broken lines alongside solid-line forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Modifications may not be shown in broken lines on figures which show in solid lines another form of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All modifications described must be illustrated or the text canceled (Ex parte Badger; Ex parte Peck). This requirement does not apply to a mere reference to minor variations nor to well-known and conventional parts. Form paragraph 6.22.05 may be used to require correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of corrections; shortened statutory periods at allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: If corrected drawings are required in an Office action or Notice of Allowability, applicant must file within the time set; certain periods are shortened and non-extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If corrected drawings are required in a Notice of Allowability (PTOL-37), the new drawings MUST be filed within the THREE MONTH shortened statutory period set for reply in the 'Notice of Allowability.' Extensions of time may NOT be obtained under 37 CFR 1.136(a) or (b). If the Office of Data Management receives drawings that cannot be scanned or are otherwise unacceptable for publication, the Office will mail a requirement giving applicant a shortened statutory period of two months (with no extensions permitted) to reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO no longer makes drawing changes; applicant responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will not make drawing changes for applicant; it is the applicant's responsibility to ensure drawings are corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 6.39 and related paragraphs remind applicant that the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office no longer makes drawing changes and that corrections must be made in accordance with provided instructions. When an applicant files a request for the Office to make drawing changes, the examiner should use form paragraph 6.40 to inform applicant that the Office no longer makes changes and that it is applicant's responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustration and labeling of prior art figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures showing prior art are usually unnecessary and should be canceled; if retained they must be labeled (e.g., '--Prior Art--').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where needed to understand applicant’s invention, prior art figures may be retained if designated by a legend such as 'Prior Art.' If the prior art figure is not labeled, form paragraph 6.36.01 may be used and Figure should be designated by a legend such as '--Prior Art--' because only that which is old is illustrated. Corrected drawings in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(d) are required in reply to the Office action to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of drawings from prior applications requires petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfer of drawings from a first pending application to another will be made only upon granting of a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 showing hardship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition must set forth a hardship situation requiring such transfer of drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation, retention, and use of drawing prints
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawing prints of acceptable drawings are made and retained for paper applications; no drawing prints are made for IFW applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prints are made of acceptable drawings maintained in paper and kept on top of the papers on the right side of the file wrapper. Original drawing should not be marked up by the examiner. Drawing prints may be used unofficially for coloring or adding legends/arrows and may be retained in the paper application file; in IFW applications the drawing prints may be retained by the examiner. Prints remain in the paper application file at all times except as provided in MPEP § 608.02(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of replacement drawing sheets; examiner must explain denial
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical support staff will enter replacement sheets; examiner must consider new matter, necessity, and consistency; if not entered, applicant must be given a concise and complete explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement drawings, together with the file wrapper, may be routed through the TC Draftsperson to identify errors. The examiner should not overlook factors such as new matter, the necessity for the replacement sheets and consistency with other sheets. The technical support staff will routinely enter replacement sheets in the contents of the application; if the examiner decides that the sheets should not be entered, the examiner should provide the applicant with the complete, explicit reasoning for the denial of entry. Entries made by technical support staff will be marked '(N.E.).'

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of figures and resulting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If a drawing figure is canceled, a replacement sheet without the figure must be submitted; if the canceled figure was the only drawing on the sheet, a marked-up copy showing cancellation is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a drawing figure is canceled, the replacement drawing sheet must be submitted without the figure (see 37 CFR 1.121(d)). If the canceled drawing figure was the only drawing on the sheet, then only a marked-up copy of the drawing sheet including an annotation showing the drawing has been canceled is required. The marked-up copy must be clearly labeled as 'Annotated Sheet' and must be presented in the amendment or remarks section which explains the changes to the drawings (see 37 CFR 1.121(d)(1)). The brief description of the drawings should also be amended to reflect this change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of drawing corrections examiners may make (illustrative list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain slight defects not involving structural change may be corrected by examiner via annotated sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a guide to the examiner, illustrative corrections that may be made by an annotated sheet include: (A) Adding two or three reference characters or exponents; (B) Changing one or two numerals or figure ordinals; (C) Removing superfluous matter; (D) Adding or reversing directional arrows; (E) Changing Roman numerals to Arabic numerals to agree with specification; (F) Adding section lines or brackets; (G) Changing lead lines; (H) Correcting misspelled legends. Where an application is ready for issue except for a slight defect in the drawing not involving change in structure, the examiner will prepare a letter indicating the change to be made and include a marked-up copy of the drawing showing the addition or alteration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing corrections accepted unless notified otherwise; examiner must explain if not accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawing corrections or changes will be entered at the time presented unless applicant is notified to the contrary; if not accepted, examiner shall explain reasons in the next communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the corrected or changed drawing is not accepted—for example, because the submitted corrections are erroneous, involve new matter, or do not include all necessary corrections—the applicant will be notified and informed of any required corrective action in the next Office action. The examiner should explicitly and clearly set forth all the reasons for not approving the corrections to the drawings in the next communication to the applicant. See MPEP § 608.02(p) for suggested form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings will not be returned to applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings will not be returned to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph and statement: 'Drawings will not be returned to the applicant.' Applicants should retain originals and expect the Office to keep submitted drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable applications needing drawing corrections; handling at allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is being allowed and corrected drawings have not been filed, PTOL-37 provides a check box for requiring corrected drawings and examiners should not require new drawings merely because applicant indicated drawings were informal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At allowance, if the examiner determines correction is required, the drawings requiring correction should be placed as the top papers in the center fold of the file wrapper for paper applications. In IFW applications, generally the most recently filed drawings will be used for printing unless they have been indicated as 'Not Entered.' Extensions of time to provide acceptable drawings after the mailing of a notice of allowability are no longer permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Models/exhibits/specimens admission criteria (37 CFR 1.91)
rubrics_metrics.description: A model or exhibit will not be admitted as part of the record of an application unless it substantially conforms to § 1.52 or § 1.84, is specifically required by the Office, or is filed with a petition including fee and explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.91(a): (1) Substantially conforms to the requirements of § 1.52 or § 1.84; (2) Is specifically required by the Office; or (3) Is filed with a petition under this section including the fee set forth in § 1.17(h) and an explanation of why entry of the model or exhibit in the file record is necessary to demonstrate patentability. Notwithstanding this, a model or other physical exhibit may be required by the Office if deemed necessary for any purpose in examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographic requirements for models or exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: Models or exhibits submitted without substantial conformity must be accompanied by photographs showing multiple views of the material features and substantially conforming to § 1.84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.91(c): Where a model or exhibit does not substantially conform to § 1.52 or § 1.84, it must be accompanied by photographs that show multiple views of the material features of the model or exhibit and that substantially conform to the requirements of § 1.84. For video/DVD submissions, applicant must submit photographs of what is depicted in the video (e.g., a still image single frame) and not a photograph of the physical media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling, labeling, storage, and demonstration of models/exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: All models and exhibits should be identified, labeled, taken to the Technology Center, and may be used in interviews but generally will not be admitted as part of the application without meeting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A label indicating application number, filing date, and attorney’s name/address should be attached to the model or exhibit. Models and exhibits presented during interviews should be taken away by applicant/agent at conclusion; any model or exhibit left with the examiner and not made part of the application may be disposed of at the Office's discretion. A full description of what was demonstrated or exhibited during the interview must be made of record (see 37 CFR 1.133). If the model cannot be conveniently stored within the file wrapper or artifact folder, it should not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return of models/exhibits/specimens and applicant obligations (37 CFR 1.94)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a model/exhibit/specimen is no longer necessary, the Office may return it but applicant must arrange return at applicant's expense within the time set, or Office may dispose of the item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.94: Applicant is given normally one month from mailing of notice to make arrangements for return (shorter for perishables). Applicant is responsible for retaining the actual item for the enforceable life of any patent resulting from the application except where exceptions apply (substantial conformity to 1.52/1.84, described by photographs, or perishable). Extensions of time are available under § 1.136 except for perishables. Failure to arrange return may permit Office to dispose of the item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies and removal of exhibits (37 CFR 1.95)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of models or other physical exhibits will not ordinarily be furnished and exhibits shall not be removed from the Office except in custody of an authorized employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.95: Copies of exhibits are not ordinarily furnished by the Office, and any model or exhibit in an application or patent shall not be taken from the Office except in the custody of an employee specially authorized by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter may be introduced in amendments (37 CFR 1.121(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may introduce new matter into the disclosure of an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When new matter is introduced into the specification, the amendment should be objected to under 35 U.S.C. 132 (35 U.S.C. 251 for reissue) and a requirement made to cancel the new matter. The subject matter considered to be new matter must be clearly identified by the examiner. If new matter has been entered into the claims or affects claim scope, the affected claims should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, because the new matter is not described in the application as originally filed. While amendments involving new matter are ordinarily entered, such matter is required to be canceled from the descriptive portion and affected claims rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of canceled figures
rubrics_metrics.description: A canceled figure may be reinstated, but an amendment should be made to the specification adding the brief description of the view if a canceled figure is reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a canceled figure is reinstated, the applicant should amend the specification to add the brief description of the view to reflect the reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notations on drawings and draftsperson stamps
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings are no longer endorsed with application number or receipt date; draftsperson approval stamps are no longer required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A draftsperson's 'stamp' to indicate approval is no longer required on patent drawings and these stamps are no longer used. If the drawings in an allowed application are not indicated as having been disapproved or canceled, the most-recently filed drawings will be used for printing the patent.
